mechanism_claims.claim_text: HR2-derived stapled peptides are curated as RSV fusion-entry inhibitors that interfere with formation of the postfusion six-helix bundle rather than as antibacterial membrane-permeabilizing AMPs.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=5:Stapled-peptide scan across the HR2 domain; xml:sec=22:5HB fluorescence polarization assay

mechanism_claims.limitations: The direct biochemical target is the RSV F HR1/HR2 fusion intermediate model; the paper does not show antibacterial killing or host membrane permeabilization as the curated mechanism.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Double stapling is necessary for potent activity in this series: 3ac inhibits RSV infection while the best single-stapled peptides do not, and optimized 4bb/4ca are the strongest Table 2 cellular inhibitors.
mechanism_claims.limitations: The source supports RSV infection inhibition and structure-activity relationships, not broad antimicrobial claims.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Ala-scanning localizes loss of antiviral activity to substitutions at residues 506 to 509, consistent with the HR2/HR1 contact model.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Exact mutant EC50 values are in an image table; local text gives the critical-residue interpretation and database rows provide the linked numeric values.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Intranasal peptide 4ca shows in vivo prophylactic antiviral effect in BALB/c mice without a numeric toxicity table; source review keeps the safety evidence qualitative.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: peptide 4ca in BALB/c mouse RSV-Luc model
mechanism_claims.limitations: This is a mouse prophylaxis/bioluminescence outcome and histology observation, not a human efficacy or immunogenicity conclusion.
